items.stem: A 7-year-old boy presented with eye strain especially after reading. His mother noticed convergent squint especially on holding his mobile. Examination using cycloplegic revealed +5.0 sphere refraction both eyes. Visual acuity both eyes was 6/6.

options.a: In this child parallel rays come to focus behind the retina if he does not accommodate.
options.c: Treating the child with convex lens is essential.
options.d: Eye strain may be due to accommodative asthenopia.

items.stem: A 14-year-old boy presented with difficulty seeing the board in classroom. A year before he got same symptoms and eyeglasses were prescribed but he did not use them. His father was wearing myopic glasses.

options.a: In this boy parallel rays come to focus behind the retina with no accommodation.
options.b: In this boy parallel rays come to focus in front of the retina with no accommodation.
options.c: Convex lenses are used for treatment.
options.d: Sometimes this boy squeezes his eyes to get pin hole effect.

items.stem: A 22-year-old male came to ophthalmology clinic complaining of blurring of vision when looking at far objects although wearing his myopic glasses since he was 7 years old. He said that the power of his glasses is increasing every year. His old glasses were -12.0 diopters bilaterally.

options.a: Your provisional diagnosis is pathological or degenerative myopia.
options.b: Short axial length of the globe is expected in this patient.
options.d: Open angle glaucoma is easy to diagnose in high myopic eyes.

items.stem: A 25-year-old female came to the clinic complaining of defective blurry vision for distant and near work with eye strain, fatigue and headache. Refraction revealed unequal values in different axes. On examination the patient can see some signs and miss others in same line.

options.a: Corneal topography may be used in diagnosis.
options.b: Retinoscopy and keratometry may be used in diagnosis.
options.c: In regular astigmatism the steep and flat axes are not perpendicular to each other.
options.d: Correction of this condition is by cylindrical lenses.

items.stem: A 45-year-old emmetropic female patient who never had to wear eyeglasses before, presented with inability to read small letters and blurred vision for near objects as sewing. Examination revealed vision for far is 6/6.

options.a: This condition is known as hypermetropia.
options.b: This is due to weakness of the ability to accommodate.
options.c: In this patient correction with concave lenses is advised.
options.d: This condition is known as presbyopia.

items.stem: A 68-year-old male came to outpatient clinic complaining of blurred vision in right eye and inability to see clearly. History of cataract operation right eye and IOL implantation 2 days before. Examination revealed corneal edema (increase in corneal thickness and haziness). Left cornea was clear.

options.a: Corneal edema may be due to damage of endothelial cells of cornea.
options.b: Corneal edema in this patient may be due to herpetic eye disease.
options.c: Fuch's dystrophy is the cause of corneal edema in this patient.
options.d: Pumping of ions and fluids out of the cornea is mostly done by epithelial cells.

items.stem: A 34-year-old female came to outpatient clinic complaining of decreased vision in left eye. The patient also complained of foreign body sensation and lacrimation of same eye. Examination revealed entropion and lashes rubbing against cornea and corneal opacity. The patient stated she got before several attacks of red eye.

options.a: Trachoma may lead to corneal opacities through repeated trauma.
options.b: Disturbance of regular stromal collagen fibers is the cause of corneal opacity.
options.c: Regular collagen fibers cause scattering of light rays.
options.d: The cause of opacity in this patient is penetrating corneal trauma.

items.stem: A 62-year-old female patient presented complaining of a red, watery eye for the past two days with stitching pain and photophobia. Her vision has dropped to 6/24. She had history of diabetes for 10 years and was taking drops for dry eye but was otherwise healthy. Slit lamp examination revealed a corneal epithelial defect with positive fluorescein staining.

options.a: Diabetes may predispose to altering corneal epithelium and Bowman's membrane.
options.b: Stem cells are important for epithelial regeneration.
options.c: Chemical injuries never affect stem cells.
options.d: Decrease vision in this patient is due to endothelial cell loss.

items.stem: A 52-year-old female patient came to outpatient clinic complaining of gradual diminution of vision both eyes specially left eye. She said that she had severe dry eye with burning sensation and was diagnosed pemphigoid. Corneal opacities were detected.

options.a: A normal tear film is essential for corneal transparency.
options.b: Surface keratinization of cornea can occur in pemphigoid.
options.c: Prolonged and severe dry eyes never cause corneal opacities.
options.d: Decrease mucin layer of tears occurs in Sjogren's syndrome.

items.stem: A 30-year-old male patient came to ophthalmology clinic complaining of bilateral blurred vision. Examination revealed bilateral symmetrical corneal opacities. He stated that his father also had poor vision.

options.a: The cause of diminution of vision in this patient is deposition of red blood cells.
options.b: The cause of diminution of vision is calcium deposition.
options.c: Corneal dystrophies affect vision depending on the layer of cornea involved.
options.d: Treatment of most corneal opacities is mainly surgical.

items.stem: A 19-year-old male was complaining of frequent changing his glasses, his refraction was -7.0 sphere -5.0 cylinder. Central corneal linear striae were seen at posterior corneal stroma. Scissoring of red reflex on retinoscopy was detected.

options.a: Soft contact lenses are the main line of treating this condition.
options.b: The vertical striae are called Vogt striae.
options.c: Vernal conjunctivitis is a common association.
options.d: Down syndrome and Marfan syndrome are never an association.

items.stem: A 28-year-old male came to emergency room complaining of acute drop of vision in his left eye. Examination revealed left corneal edema and right eye shows Munson sign. The patient stated he was previously diagnosed as keratoconus.

options.b: The cause of acute drop of vision is due to excess stretching of Descemet's membrane.
options.c: Corneal collagen cross linking is used in treatment of keratoconus.
options.d: Keratoplasty is never used in management of keratoconus.

items.stem: A 73-year-old female came complaining of glare and gradual painless decrease in vision of her right eye. She gave no history of systemic or local diseases in eye. Examination revealed clear cornea. The red reflex showed black sectors and vision of right eye was 5/60 and 6/18 left eye.

options.a: The patient may have immature senile cataract.
options.b: Most common cause of cataract is congenital cataract.
options.c: The patient may be diagnosed as mature cataract.
options.d: Uveitis is the cause of decreased vision in this patient.

items.stem: A 78-year-old male patient came to ophthalmology clinic. The patient complaint was gradual painless progressive diminution of vision in his left eye for 2 years. The patient gave no history of local or systemic disease. Examination revealed vision was hand movement in left eye compared to 4/60 right eye. The left red reflex appeared white. The left capsule was glistening, and the anterior chamber was shallow.

options.a: The most probable diagnosis is left nuclear cataract.
options.b: The most probable diagnosis is left intumescent cataract.
options.c: The IOP intraocular pressure may become acutely elevated.
options.d: Cataract surgery may be postponed for one year.

items.stem: A 45-year-old male was referred from dermatology clinic to ophthalmology clinic because of diminution of vision in both eyes. He was diagnosed as Behcet's disease and got recurrent attacks of iritis. Examination revealed iris pigments on anterior capsule of partially opaque lens. The pupil was festooned due to posterior synechia. Vision was hand movement in right eye and 3/60 in left eye.

options.b: Prolonged topical use of steroids never causes cataract.
options.c: Ultrasonography in this patient is essential.
options.d: Light projection and discrimination of colors are of no value.

items.stem: A 19-year-old boy came to the ophthalmic clinic due to rapid drop of vision of his right eye after being hit by squash ball 2 weeks before. Examination revealed vision 2/60 in right eye and 6/6 in left eye. The lens was partially opaque. The globe was intact with no signs of rupture.

options.b: Fundus examination and ultrasound are essential.
options.c: Medical treatment is the main line for treatment.
options.d: Complete systematic eye examination is essential.
